newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yields close higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yields close higher in thin trade.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

---------------------------(Jan 27)----------------------------- * NZ yields continue to rise in response to weaker Kiwi
* Trade very light with Australia, Auckland out on holidays
* Worse than expected current account data bearish
New Zealand debt securities closed weaker on Monday although the Australia Day and Auckland Anniversary holidays conspired against significant volumes.
Dealers said yields in the money market continued to drift higher in response the currency's one US cent fall on Friday, with the 90-day rate up six points to 7.52 percent.
One dealer said some investors may have been disappointed that the currency hadn't recovered.

"I think probably on Friday afternoon there was a bit of a feeling that the Kiwi had been oversold...there really hasn't been much movement in the currency (since then) so that's probably just disappointed a few people," he said.

Yields in the bond market rose around four points across the curve in very light trade. Dealers said weaker offshore markets on Friday had set the tone, but worse-than-expected September quarter current account data contributed to the negative sentiment.

Statistics New Zealand said the current account deficit for the September quarter was $2.17 billion, bringing the September annual balance of payments deficit to NZ$4.2 billion, or 4.6 percent of GDP, the worst result since 1987.
Economists had forecast a quarterly deficit of $1.71 billion and an annual deficit of $3.71 billion.
"It added to the bearish sentiment, it moved things say another point," said a dealer.
